avg_teacher_rating.name: avg_teacher_rating
avg_teacher_rating.definition: Arithmetic mean of TeacherRating across unique instructors.
avg_teacher_rating.caveat: Evaluation reflects student perception of instructor directly.

avg_course_rating.name: avg_course_rating
avg_course_rating.definition: Arithmetic mean of CourseRating across unique course catalog titles.
avg_course_rating.caveat: Independent of enrollment volumes; reflects catalog baseline quality.

rating_consistency_index.name: rating_consistency_index
rating_consistency_index.definition: Enrollment-weighted mean of per-instructor course quality consistency (1 - CV_weighted).
rating_consistency_index.caveat: Instructors teaching a wider diversity of subjects naturally display wider variation.

experience_impact.name: experience_impact
experience_impact.definition: Annual rating increase per year of instructor teaching experience.
experience_impact.caveat: Experience strongly predicts teacher rating but has negligible translation into course quality.

enrollment_influence.name: enrollment_influence
enrollment_influence.definition: Ratio of high-tier enrollment share to instructor population representation.
enrollment_influence.caveat: Top superstar instructors skew platform volume; see leave-top-k sensitivity.

F1.question: What are the distributional characteristics and normality of instructor ratings?
F1.method: Summary stats, Shapiro-Wilk normality test, Bootstrap CIs
F1.notes: Instructor ratings average 3.12 (median 3.28, IQR 1.34, skewness -0.48). Shapiro-Wilk normality test: W=0.962, p=0.0583.

F2.question: Does instructor experience predict higher instructor rating?
F2.method: Pearson r (Fisher-z CI), Spearman rho, OLS linear slope
F2.notes: Experience is positively correlated with TeacherRating (r = 0.598, p = 4.5176e-07, slope = 0.120 rating points/year). Excluding >=15 yrs yields r = 0.553 (p = 8.2893e-06).

F3.question: Does instructor experience transfer to higher course ratings?
F3.method: Teacher-level Pearson r vs Pair-level Cluster-Robust OLS
F3.notes: At teacher level (n=60), experience vs weighted course rating is r = -0.057 (p = 0.6659, negligible effect). At pair level (n=887), naive p-value is 6.9602e-01, but cluster-robust standard errors yield p = 0.3566.

F4.question: Is there an experience threshold or nonlinear plateau in instructor ratings?
F4.method: Two-group Mann-Whitney U, Piecewise OLS threshold search, LOWESS smoother
F4.notes: 0-5 yrs vs 6+ yrs: mean diff = +1.36 rating points (Mann-Whitney U = 839.0, p = 7.1863e-09, r_rb = -0.87). Threshold search indicates candidate inflection at b=8 yrs (delta-R2 = 0.0636, perm p = 0.1279).

F5.question: Are instructor ratings correlated with the quality ratings of the courses they teach?
F5.method: Multi-level correlation (Teacher n=60, Course n=60, Pair n=887 with cluster-robust SE)
F5.notes: Teacher-level correlation is r = 0.000 (p = 0.9971). Course-level correlation is r = -0.013 (p = 0.9212). Instructor performance and course quality are statistically decoupled (rating_decoupling = True).

F6.question: Do course quality ratings differ significantly across course categories?
F6.method: Kruskal-Wallis H test with epsilon-squared effect and Holm post-hoc
F6.notes: Kruskal-Wallis across course categories: H = 4.388, p = 9.5716e-01, epsilon^2 = 0.000 (negligible effect). 29 cells in Category x Level have n < 3.

F7.question: Do course quality ratings vary by course difficulty level?
F7.method: Kruskal-Wallis across levels and Mann-Whitney U for Advanced vs Intermediate
F7.notes: Kruskal-Wallis across levels: H = 1.913, p = 3.8423e-01, epsilon^2 = 0.000. Advanced vs Intermediate contrast: mean diff = -0.51 (p = 0.1468, r_rb = 0.28).

F8.question: Do instructor ratings or course quality vary by gender and course level?
F8.method: Teacher-level Mann-Whitney U & Transaction-level cluster-bootstrapped cells
F8.notes: At teacher level (n=60), TeacherRating does not differ significantly by Gender (Female vs Male Mann-Whitney p = 0.1187, r_rb = -0.24). Weighted course rating by Gender also shows p = 0.0045. Gender x Level differences in transactions are descriptive and reflect assignment distributions.

F9.question: Do High-tier instructors teach higher-rated courses than Mid or Low-tier instructors?
F9.method: Kruskal-Wallis across tiers on teacher_table with Holm post-hoc
F9.notes: Kruskal-Wallis across instructor tiers: H = 0.068, p = 0.9668, epsilon^2 = 0.000. Tier means on weighted course rating: High=3.17, Mid=3.14, Low=3.17.

F10.question: Do higher-rated instructors attract significantly more student enrollments?
F10.method: Teacher-level Spearman rho with bootstrap CI and High-tier vs rest contrast
F10.notes: Spearman correlation between TeacherRating and total enrollments is rho = -0.012 (p = 0.9274). High-tier instructors average 620.0 enrollments vs 64.9 for rest (Mann-Whitney p = 0.0301).

F11.question: Is enrollment driven by instructor rating or concentrated in specific domains?
F11.method: Inequality indices (Gini, Top-N, HHI), Leave-k-out sensitivity, Robust domain-controlled OLS
F11.notes: Teacher enrollment Gini = 0.681, Top-5 share = 65.5%, HHI = 1885.7. Controlling for domain in OLS (HC3), TeacherRating slope on log(enr) is beta = 0.164 (p = 0.3823, partial R2 = 0.027).

F12.question: Do instructor ratings vary systematically across expertise domains?
F12.method: Kruskal-Wallis H test across domains meeting sample size threshold
F12.notes: Kruskal-Wallis across 9 expertise areas with n >= 3: H = 15.196, p = 0.0554, epsilon^2 = 0.153. Excluded due to small sample size: ['Business', 'Marketing', 'Programming'].

F13.question: How does course quality vary by expertise domain, and is there an ML curriculum gap?
F13.method: Domain-specific aggregation, cluster CIs, and ML curriculum gap contrast
F13.notes: Machine Learning Curriculum Gap: ML instructor ratings are high (mean = 4.23), whereas ML course catalog quality is low (mean = 2.66), creating an evidence gap of +1.58 rating points. Mean own-domain teaching share across platform is 74.0%.
